_comment: Host-specific BLFS review decisions for `server`. Merged on top of recipes/blfs-overrides.json by bin/extract-blfs.py, page by page and block by block, so a page keeps its shared decisions and takes only the hardware-bound ones from here. Every entry must name a concrete GPU, CPU, device or path -- if a decision is true of any LFS box, it belongs in the shared file.

2.cmd:
mkdir build &&
cd    build &&

meson setup ..                    \
      --prefix=$XORG_PREFIX       \
      --buildtype=release         \
      -D platforms=x11,wayland    \
      -D gallium-drivers=nouveau  \
      -D vulkan-drivers=nouveau   \
      -D valgrind=disabled        \
      -D video-codecs=all         \
      -D libunwind=disabled       \
      -D glvnd=enabled           &&

ninja
2.reason:
Driver scope and the glvnd/Vulkan options are bound to this machine's GPU, so they live here rather than in the shared file. This block is the only reason blfs-mesa is a host recipe at all.

gallium-drivers=nouveau (book default: auto). Decided with the operator 2026-08-25: this box's only GPU is a GTX 770 (GK104, Kepler). auto builds every vendor's driver -- AMD (r300/r600/radeonsi), Intel (iris/crocus), virgl, svga -- none of which this hardware will ever use. nouveau covers the real GPU; llvmpipe is the book's own recommended software-rendering backup and comes in regardless.

vulkan-drivers=nouveau (was empty, then enabled on the 2026-08-26 rebuild). NVK, Mesa's Vulkan driver for NVIDIA hardware, officially supports Kepler (GeForce 600/700, this card included) per Mesa's own docs -- not experimental for this GPU. Needs Linux 6.6+ (this system runs 6.18.10). Kepler is capped at Vulkan 1.2 by hardware (no vulkanMemoryModel, required for 1.3+) even though NVK claims 1.4 conformance for newer generations: a hardware ceiling, not a driver gap. NVK does not share code with the gallium state tracker -- the OpenGL/VAAPI path that has a confirmed crash bug on this card (see BUILD-REPORT.md's GPU deep-dive) -- so that bug does not carry over. vulkan-loader was already installed; the book's circular-dependency note is about libva and does not apply here.

glvnd=enabled (book default: auto), added on the 2026-08-26 rebuild. This is a meson type:feature option, and Mesa was originally built before libglvnd existed, so auto detected no glvnd and defaulted to disabled -- Mesa installed a standalone libEGL.so.1.0.0 with no glvnd vendor ABI. libglvnd's own libEGL.so.1.1.0 later won the /usr/lib/libEGL.so.1 soname, with no vendor JSON in /usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d telling it where to dispatch, so real EGL calls had nothing behind them. A hand-written vendor JSON cannot fix it: the standalone libEGL.so.1.0.0 implements only the direct EGL ABI, not glvnd's vendor entry points. A Mesa rebuild is the only fix. Anything building Mesa alongside libglvnd needs this option set explicitly rather than left on auto, whatever the GPU -- the ordering trap is not NVIDIA-specific.

GLX needs no equivalent option (checked 2026-08-26, no rebuild): Mesa's src/glx/meson.build has no vendor-JSON step at all, it only builds libGLX_mesa.so.0 under glvnd. libglvnd's GLX vendor selection is file-less -- libGLX.so queries the X server per screen via the GLX_EXT_libglvnd extension. That mattered under XWayland, which does not implement the extension and needed __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=mesa in the session launcher; it is moot now that this box runs a real Xorg server, and is recorded only because it explains why no GLX option appears above.

platforms=x11,wayland is the book default and is left alone deliberately. This box abandoned Wayland (see AWESOME-X11-PLAN.md), so the wayland platform is dead weight here, but dropping it would mean rebuilding Mesa to match a recipe change that buys nothing. Recorded as a known, deliberate no-op rather than silently trimmed.
